paper.title: On Frequentist Regret of Linear Thompson Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit with changing action sets
unmapped: Action sets A_t are random compact subsets of R^d that change over time
Parameter Theta* may be random (Bayesian regret); frequentist regret obtained with point-mass prior
||A||_2 <= a for all actions a.s.; ||Theta*||_2 <= theta (used in confidence radius rho)
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\ArmSet_t)_{t=1}^T$ be a sequence of $T$ random compact subsets of $\IR^d$ where $T\in\IN$ is the time horizon. We further assume that $\Norm{\Arm}_2\leq\ArmBound$ for all $\Arm\in\ArmSet_t$ almost surely. ... receives a stochastic reward $\RewardValue_t=\Inner[\big]{\Param,\ChosenArm_t}+\eps_t$ where $\eps_t$ is the reward noise and $\Param$ is an unknown (and potentially random) vector of parameters.

settings.name_in_paper: Examples 1 and 2: linear bandit with Gaussian prior/noise mismatched to LinTS's assumed N(0,1)
unmapped: Bayesian regret with Gaussian prior Theta* ~ N(0, sigma^2 I) (Ex.1) or N(mu 1, sigma^2 I) / N(0, sigma^2 I + rho 11^T) (Ex.2)
Gaussian noise N(0, tau^2); LinTS assumes prior and noise variance 1 (misspecified)
Action sets constructed in advance (Example 1: changing; Example 2: fixed set {0, A', A})
Lower bounds are specific to LinTS without inflation
settings.definition_quote: Fix $\sigma^2,\tau^2\geq 0$ and let $\Param\sim\Normal{0,\sigma^2\II_2}$ be the vector of unobserved parameters. ... Assume that reward $Y_t=\Param_t+\eps_t$ is revealed to the algorithm where $\eps_t\sim\Normal{0,\tau^2}$.

algorithms.name: LinTS (Linear Thompson sampling with inflation iota)
OFUL with smaller confidence sets (ROFUL instance)

symbols.rho: confidence radius with ||hat Theta_t - Theta*||_{Sigma_t^{-1}} <= rho
symbols.p_opt: lower bound on probability of optimism

extra_assumptions: Optimism condition: P(sup <A,tilde Theta_t> >= sup <A,Theta*> | Theta*, F_t) >= p whenever ||hat Theta_t - Theta*||_{Sigma_t^{-1}} <= rho

source.label: thm:expected-regret-bound
source.quote: If \cref{alg:proper-ts} satisfies \Prob*{ \sup_{\Arm\in\ArmSet_t}\Inner{\Arm,\TsSample_t} \geq \sup_{\Arm\in\ArmSet_t}\Inner{\Arm,\Param} \Given \Param,\HistoryPlus_t } \geq \OptProb, whenever $\Norm{\Estimator_t-\Param}_{\SymCovMatrix_t^{-1}}\leq\Radius$, we then have \Regret(T,\PolicyTS) \leq \OrderLog*{\frac{\Radius\Inflation}{\OptProb}\sqrt{\Dim T}}.

results.notes: Regret defined as Bayesian regret (expectation including prior). Conditional sufficient-condition result.

symbols.sigma: true prior std (in this paper sigma is the prior std, not noise)

extra_assumptions: LinTS with iota=1, lambda=1 (assumes unit prior and noise variance)

source.label: prop:noise-reduction-failure
source.quote: In Example 1, when $\sigma\neq\tau$ and $T\leq\exp(\LowerOrder{d})$, we have $\Regret(T,\PolicyTS) \geq \LowerOrder{T}\,.$

results.notes: Lower bound applies to LinTS without inflation only.

source.label: cor:noise-reduction-failure
source.quote: In Example 1, when $d=\LowerOrder{\log T}$ and $\sigma\neq\tau$, we have \Regret(T,\PolicyTS) \geq \LowerOrder{T}\,.

bound.regime: T <= exp(Omega(d)), d sufficiently large, fixed mu, sigma > 0

extra_assumptions: Example 2: fixed action set {0, A', A}, prior N(mu 1, sigma^2 I)

source.label: prop:mean-shift-failure
source.quote: For fixed $\mu,\sigma>0$, and for sufficiently large $d$, we have ... For all $T\leq\exp(\LowerOrder{d})$, $\Regret(T,\PolicyTS)\geq\LowerOrder{T\sqrt d}$.

results.notes: Actions have norm up to sqrt(3), rewards scale with sqrt(d).

extra_assumptions: Example 2, prior N(mu 1, sigma^2 I) or N(0, sigma^2 I + rho 11^T)

source.label: cor:mean-shift-failure
source.quote: In Example 2, when $d=\LowerOrder{\log T}$ and the true prior $\Prior$ is either $\Normal{\mu\One_{3d},\sigma^2\II_{3d}}$ or $\Prior=\Normal{0,\sigma^2\II_{3d}+\rho\One_{3d}\One_{3d}^\top}$, we have \Regret(T,\PolicyTS) \geq \LowerOrder{T}\,.

symbols.N_thin: number of rounds with thinness psi(Sigma_t) > Psi

source.label: thm:lin-ts-regret-informal
source.quote: Assume that $\Inner{\Arm,\Param}\in[-1,1]$ for all $\Arm\in\ArmSet_t$ almost surely. Then, under \cref{as:optimal-diversity,as:optimal-random-friendly}, we have \sum_{t=1}^T \Inner{\OptimalArm_t,\Param}-\Inner{\ChosenArm_t,\Param} \leq \OrderLog{\Inflation\Dim\sqrt{T}} + 2 \sum_{t=1}^{T}\Indicator(\Thinness(\SymCovMatrix_t)>\ThinnessBound)\,, with probability at least $1-\frac3T$, provided that ... $\Inflation\geq\frac{\DivParam\ThinnessBound}{\ExploreRatio}\cdot\OrderLog{1}$.

results.notes: Informal statement; bound contains data-dependent term N_thin. Realized regret sum w.r.t. means.

symbols.N_thin: number of rounds with thinness psi(Sigma_t) > Psi

extra_assumptions: Worth function optimistic with parameter p

source.label: thm:lin-ts-regret
source.quote: Let $\Worth_t(\cdot)$ be optimistic with parameter $\OptProb$ whenever $\ITypical_t=1$, $\ITypicalM_t=1$, and $\IWellPosed_t=1$. When \cref{as:optimal-diversity,as:optimal-random-friendly} hold, and $\Inner{\Arm,\Param}\in[-1,1]$, ... Then, we have that \sum_{t=1}^{T}\Inner[\big]{\Param,\OptimalArm_t}-\Inner[\big]{\Param,\ChosenArm_t} \leq \frac{4(\RadiusParam+\RadiusWorth)\sqrt T}{\OptProb} (...) +2\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Indicator(\Thinness(\SymCovMatrix_t)>\ThinnessBound)\,, with probability at least $1-\frac3T$.

results.notes: Generic ROFUL meta-algorithm bound. L_feat = a (action norm bound).

symbols.N_thin: number of rounds with thinness psi(Sigma_t) > Psi

source.label: cor:lin-ts-regret
source.quote: Consider \LinTS{} with inflation parameter $\Inflation$ satisfying \Inflation=\frac{\DivParam\ThinnessBound}{\ExploreRatio}\cdot\frac{\Radius}{\sqrt{d}} and \frac{\RadiusWorth}{\Inflation}=\LowerOrder{\sqrt{\log T}}. Then, when \cref{as:optimal-diversity,as:optimal-random-friendly} hold, the regret is at most ... with probability at least $1-\frac3T$.

results.notes: Corollary numbering approximate. LinTS run within ROFUL (arbitrary action when thinness exceeds Psi).

Then, when \cref{as:optimal-diversity,as:optimal-random-friendly} hold, the regret is at most ... with probability at least $1-\frac3T$.
